pr_title: Fix IpSubnetFilterRule with IPv6 Default Route does not accept all IPv6 addresses
pr_body:
Motivation:

In this issue(https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11349 ),IpSubnetFilterRule needs to support ipv6 reserved addresses, such as 8000::, but the current implementation does not support

Modification:

Added support for default rule

Result:

Fixes https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/11349

issue_context.title: IpSubnetFilterRule with IPv6 Default Route does not accept all IPv6 addresses
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior
I would expect that creating an accepting IpSubnetFilterRule with the IPv6 default route ("::/0")  should accept any IPv6 address, just like it does for IPv4.

### Actual behavior
Any IPv6 address higher than 7FFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF is rejected, however anything below that address and including it appears to be valid.

### Steps to reproduce
Create an IpSubnetFilterRule with the IPv6 default route and create a test trying to match an IPv6 of 8000:: or higher.

### Minimal yet complete reproducer code (or URL to code)
    IpFilterRule rule = new IpSubnetFilterRule("::", 0, IpFilterRuleType.ACCEPT);
    assertTrue(rule.matches(new InetSocketAddress("7FFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF:FFFF", 0))); // this is okay
    assertTrue(rule.matches(new InetSocketAddress("8000::", 0))); // this fails

### Netty version
4.1.51

### JVM version (e.g. `java -version`)
1.8.201

### OS version (e.g. `uname -a`)
Windows 10
